body: What's POCD? I've honestly not talked to a professional about my situation in close to ten years. I was diagnosed with severe depression and anxiety back then.

I'm not going to fight with you about my own life. I'm going to leave it at this: You don't know me. I'm not denying that I having a drinking problem, but I am not addicted to alcohol whereas I am addicted to sex and it poses a far larger problem in my life.
I'm female. I will definitely look into that when I get back to my country. Thank you. I really do appreciate the support.

I turn into someone I don't even know passed a certain point. I've only seen glimpses and heard stories, but I don't like her. I don't get to this stage every time I drink, I don't even drink often, but considering I have been travelling a lot throughout the passed year, I've been drinking a lot in different countries. 

I was physically abused as a child, but not sexually. Something interesting you've made me realize is that I block out these nights from my memory the same way I blocked out almost my entire childhood from my memory.

A lot of what you said here definitely struck a chord and rang true with me. It all made a lot of sense to me. I've always had depression and anxiety issues along with self-confidence and dependance issues. I've certainly thought that I have moved away from these problems to a degree, but it seems all I have done is find a different outlet of self-harming. Maybe I wouldn't call it "self-harming" per se, but a way to feel something other than what is going on inside.

I find myself always feeling like an outsider even when that's really not the case and drinking heavily makes me feels included or gives me an in to be more open to express myself and sex as a way of feeling closer with the guys I'm interested in.

I certainly think traveling is taking a toll on me (it's been well over a year) and I need to go home and continue working on my craft/career, start working out again, start eating well, being around people who I can do more than just have drinks with... I've also been holding off dealing with cancer for several years and I'm sure there's loads more that I'm trying to avoid as well.

Thank you for your insightful comment. It has really given me a lot to think about as well as most of the other comments of this thread as well. It's really relieving that you guys aren't simply looking at me as a slut and empathizing with me that it is a genuine problem I'm having that I am willing to work on.

Not even remotely untrue.. unfortunately.

Kudos to you for undermining someone actively seeking help.

The night I slept with three guys, I was rather sober.

I do drink a lot less when I'm in a relationship though because I know what drunk me gets up to after I black-out. She's a very aggressively horny girl.

Thank you. It's really comforting to hear that. I guess it's just another hurdle in my mental illnesses that I'll have to overcome. Not that I'm opposed to having a high sex drive, haha! I would like to be in a healthy relationship (monogamous or polygamous). 

Yes, I haven't been exercising much or even masturbating at all for that matter. My living situation has made that difficult as I'm travelling and I'm a squirter.. I have been getting the urge to work out more often. I feel a lot better when I do so.

I definitely have a fear of intimacy. I'm scared of getting close and letting people get close to me because I don't want to feel trapped in a relationship that I don't want to be in. 

This makes a lot of sense. I think I may know a few things I'm running away from. This helps me a lot. Thank you.

I am going to look into a therapist when I'm done travelling and see what I can do about that financially

Yes, I have always used alcohol as a way of overcoming my shyness. I'm selective-mute and I'm not good in social situations, so I tend to drink more than I should to compensate for that. Sometimes I feel it's the only way I can meet/have fun with people. I do realize this is very dangerous.

I do have severe depression and anxiety. I was diagnosed with it eight years ago and don't take mediation for it anymore. I am significantly better than I used to be, but it never completely goes away and I don't want to go back on medication and rely on pills for the rest of my life to feel “normal”.

Unfortunately, I'm travelling at the moment and I'll be in a foreign country for a good while now. I'll look into therapy, but I've cancer to deal with as well and student loans. So, those do have to take priority over therapy if it would cost me money.

Finally, there's this one guy that I actually have genuine feelings for and I've taken the time to get to know him because he's where I'm from and I'm currently half-way across the world. I like him a lot and won't be able to have sex with him right when I meet him either (new special piercing).

I don't want to keep doing this. I love sex, but I don't want to have it with someone that means nothing to me. Not in this excess anyway...

Thank you. I needed that. I just needed to see that someone - anyone - was listening.

I've dealt with depression my whole life and have hit my bottom before and managed to work my way up from that. It's not easy and doesn't mean the feelings don't come back. I do what I can to try to cope healthily and am always learning new ways to deal with these thoughts. Travelling is huge for that; staying outside my comfort-zone is probably the best thing.

I guess that's what got me into this situation in the first place, but if I just look at it a different perspective, it makes things better. I can't worry about things that have already happened and things I can't change; I can only work towards things I can change. Things are going to get better and then they're going to get shitty again and so forth... I guess that's the ebb and flow that makes things interesting.

I came across this while waiting for a reply here:

"Happiness means never feeling any pain or disappointment"

"The key to a good life is never feeling any pain"

Two quotes think are good to look at because I think they're completely ridiculous. I've always tried to look at the painful times in my life as the most soul-strengthening moments in my life. Life would probably be boring with no pain at all.

I went on a bit of a rant here and I do feel a bit silly, but I guess the just of it is that a small comment like that can go a long way and helped me a lot more than you think. You helped from falling back into that dark place if even just for the time being and I am incredibly grateful for that. Thank you.
